thread:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: P1 - API latency spike (west1) - pages triggered. Error rate + tail latency > 3s for last 10m. Paging policy invoked. https://incidents.redwood.local/INC-20260315-42

Joan: taking this for the last 35m, handing over now — primary driver. Actions so far: rolled back canary -> v2.1.3, scaled webpool from 6->12, disabled new cache sharding flag. Customers seeing increased request timeouts.

Alex M: hi — i'm on shift now, picking this up. who is comms? any immediate blockers?

Joan: @Samir has been handling comms (sending status updates). No hotfix deployed other than rollback. We saw error bursts from instance 10 in webpool, suspect oom/kprobe. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.local/api-latency-spike

Samir: confirmed, I'm on comms. Draft posted to #customers-status: "Investigating intermittent API timeouts in west1; service degradation for some customers. Engineers assessing; ETA 30m." Will ping AEs for impacted accounts.

Alex M: ok I'm taking driver. Samir you remain comms. Nina, can you be secondary for the next hour?

Nina: I can be secondary until 06:00 UTC.

Joan: quick checklist for handoff 
- watch grafana: panels: api.latency.p50/p95/p99 + error-rate
- check pods: `kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=web -o wide`
- look at envoy logs for 502s: `kubectl logs <pod> -c envoy | grep 502`
- if error originates from webpool instance -> cordon + recreate pod

Alex M: running checks now. grabbing envoy tails + kube status.

Alex M: command I ran: 
```
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=web
kubectl -n prod logs web-10 -c app --since=15m | head -n 200
curl -sS https://metrics.redwood.local/api/latency?region=west1 | jq .p99
```
Results: web-10 shows repeated OOMKilled restarts, p99 ~3.8s. restarting that node doesn't help; suspect bad GC pattern in v2.1.3 canary (which we rolled back).

SRE Bot: automated note - observed 38% drop in error-rate after canary rollback (10m window). Continuing monitoring.

Alex M: mitigation plan: keep scaled replicas (12), cordon web-10 and drain: `kubectl drain web-10 --ignore-daemonsets --force`. If more pods spike, revert to older instance type/force new rollout. Samir post update after drain completes.

Samir: posting update to customers now. Also pinging AE #ae-east to flag 3 accounts with latency > 2s. Draft snippet: "We mitigated a canary-related latency regression by rolling back yesterday's canary; additional scaling applied. We're monitoring and will update in 15m."

Joan: one more: if scaling doesn't reduce tail latency within 10m, escalate to infra (paging policy) and consider temporary traffic steering to eu-region. runbook step 4.a covers traffic-steer commands.

Alex M: noted. small coverage gap: my shift fully overlaps Joan until 02:30 UTC, but the next oncall rotation starts at 02:50 UTC — 20m gap unless someone holds. Nina can you extend to 02:50?

Nina: I can extend to 02:50, no problem.

Incident Bot: Reminder: if P1 remains unresolved for >15m from now, auto-escalate to oncall-manager and infra-leads.

Alex M: ack. running drain now, will watch p99. If p99 stays >3s after drain + 10m, we'll prepare traffic-steer to eu as contingency.

(5m later)

SRE Bot: update: error-rate down 52%, p99 reduced to 1.2s across west1 for last 3m.

Alex M: nice. Samir post customer update that latency is improving and we're keeping scaled capacity for stability. I'll keep driving until metrics stable for 30m, then coordinate postmortem.

Joan: handing off completed — leaving for the day. Notes added to the incident log: rollback, scale, drained web-10, comms handoff.

Samir: update posted. will follow up in incident channel if any customers ask for details.

Nina: staying on for overlap, will pick up if numbers bounce back.

Alex M: thanks everyone. I'll create an incident timeline and assign postmortem owner (prob Joan or me). If anyone sees regression, ping me directly @alex_m or page via standard P1 route. :thumbsup:
